article:
We recently finished an exterior painting project on a flip property in South Loveland -- a small garage and outbuilding that needed fresh vinyl siding paint to bring out the home's character. The homeowner wanted a black accent, but here's where Northern Colorado's climate taught us something most painters miss: you can't just paint vinyl black in the Colorado sun without consequences. This project shows exactly why prep knowledge and the right paint choices matter more than most contractors admit.

What We Did

The scope was straightforward on paper -- paint the vinyl exterior of a small outbuilding in white with dark accents. We worked with Sherwin-Williams products, which is our standard for exterior work. Here's the critical detail: Sherwin-Williams won't even tint their vinyl paint black. Not because they can't, but because they won't. And we listened to why.

Our crew applied the paint over the last couple days, keeping every stroke clean and controlled. We used a dark gray instead of true black on the accent areas. That's not a compromise on aesthetics -- it's respecting Colorado's intensity. The application itself was flawless, but the color decision is what separates contractors who think ahead from those who don't.

Why Prep Matters More Than Paint

Here's the thing about vinyl: it expands and contracts with temperature. In Northern Colorado, where summer heat can be brutal and relentless, a true black vinyl paint absorbs so much solar radiation that it will actually warp and melt the siding beneath it. You could love the color on day one and watch it fail by August.

This is why we partner with Sherwin-Williams and Benjamin Moore -- suppliers who educate us on what works and what doesn't in our climate. Not every paint company will tell you this. Some will just sell you black paint and let you learn the hard way.

Beyond color selection, we treated the site like it matters. This is a flip property in someone's neighborhood. We controlled overspray meticulously, protected neighboring properties and vehicles, and kept the landscape undisturbed. That's not extra -- that's baseline for licensed and insured work in Northern Colorado, and it's why our $1M liability coverage isn't just a number on a certificate.

The Result

A crisp, clean exterior that will hold up through Colorado's temperature swings without warping, fading prematurely, or requiring early repainting. The dark gray accent reads as bold and intentional -- not a compromise, but a smart choice for durability. The homeowner gets a property that looks polished and will perform reliably for years.

That's what happens when a contractor knows their region, knows their products, and knows how to think past the first coat.

If you're planning exterior or interior painting in Northern Colorado -- whether it's a full home, an investment flip, HOA work, or commercial space -- reach out for a quote. We'll give you honest advice about what works here, not just what you want to hear.
